problem: Workflows. Three fc-* scripts exist under flightcrew/workflows (explore, implement, review) and two build scripts under .claude/workflows written for the v1 build. The core spec replaces them with a suite of workflows driven by liftoffs. Round 1 also decided this launch's own run is conducted by a workflow you ask Claude to run directly.

questions.text: Are the existing workflow scripts goes entirely, or do the behaviours inside fc-implement count as kept?
questions.why: fc-implement already does pilot-first, chunked fan-out, stop on a red return and validated returns. If those are the behaviours the new build workflow must reproduce, characterizing them now against fc-implement gives the rebuild a target; if the scripts are simply replaced, nothing is pinned.

options.value: Kept behaviours: characterize pilot-first, fan-out in chunks, stop on red, and return validation against fc-implement as it stands.
Goes entirely: no workflow behaviour is characterized; the core spec defines the new suite from scratch.

questions.text: The workflow authoring contract (meta literal first, no filesystem, shell, clock or randomness, args binding, return shapes inlined as literals) is enforced today by a static scan. Is that contract a kept rule the suite pins?
questions.why: It is a harness constraint rather than flightcrew's invention, and every future workflow must satisfy it; a static scan is cheap and deterministic.

options.value: Kept: pin the authoring contract with a static scan over every workflow file present.
Not in this suite; the runtime already enforces it.

questions.text: Which workflow conducts this launch's own run?
questions.why: Round 1 chose a directly invoked workflow over the v1 tooling. The v1 suites were built by a hand-written flightcrew-targets.js with five test-builders in parallel, each refuted and fixed once; fc-implement expects a plan and rendered dispatches.

options.value: A hand-written workflow for this run in the shape of flightcrew-targets.js: fixtures first, then test-builders in parallel each refuted once.
fc-implement, fed units and rendered dispatches, so the run also exercises the existing workflow.
